Webinar | September 1, 2026 Improved Clearance Of Host Cell Proteins After Virus Inactivation Source: Cytiva Post-viral inactivation filtration can do more than remove precipitates. When carefully developed, it may also reduce residual host cell proteins before polishing chromatography, including lipases that can compromise monoclonal antibody stability. Selecting the right filtration approach requires a close look at several competing priorities: impurity clearance, process fluid throughput, and overall cost. See how multiple Seitz filter media with different charge characteristics and an anion exchange membrane were evaluated using two distinct feeds. The findings illustrate how feed properties and media selection can influence filtration performance and help shape a more reliable, scalable purification process. access the Webinar! Application Note Don't Intensify Blindly: Preventing Fouling And Restoring Performance With Targeted Cleaning Of Protein A Resins Source: Cytiva Chromatography intensification can improve productivity and resin utilization, but greater efficiency may introduce new risks to process robustness. Protein A capture presents distinct challenges, including balancing loading capacity, residence time, cycle count, column format, and operational consistency. Understanding how these factors interact is essential when determining whether an intensified approach can meet performance expectations without creating unnecessary process complexity or variability. Explore the practical considerations behind intensified protein A protocols, the tradeoffs that can influence outcomes, and the questions teams should ask before adopting a new strategy. access the Application Note! A comparison of filtration strategies for neutralized viral inactivation pools examines how different approaches balance these competing priorities. Explore how filter selection and process design influence impurity clearance and filtration performance, with practical insights into the trade-offs that can shape downstream bioprocessing decisions. The findings can help teams evaluate strategies for achieving effective HCP reduction while maintaining an efficient, scalable workflow. Explore how filter selection and process design influence impurity clearance and filtration performance, with practical insights into the trade-offs that can shape downstream bioprocessing decisions. The findings can help teams evaluate strategies for achieving effective HCP reduction while maintaining an efficient, scalable workflow.
